attacks.detail: run() is a closed while-time-deadline loop that calls prov.ask and execute with no input()/sys.stdin. claude_interventions is assigned 0 and never incremented. Autonomy is time-bounded by --minutes; a caller must reinvoke the process, but nothing inside the loop blocks on one.
missing selected_work returns empty accepted/rejected with counts; crash 1 is fixed
selected_work as a dict is coerced to a one-item list; crash 2 is fixed
validate(None) carries n_accepted/n_rejected; crash 3 is fixed

validation.why: reply did not parse as a JSON object

attacks.detail: params as a list was rejected without raising
params as a string was rejected without raising
execute() json.loads the last stdout line; if that JSON is a list, run()'s results_summary does result.get('damage') and crashes. AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'

an unsupported type is appended to rejected with why '... is not an executable work type'. It is recorded, not lost. The live comment names this UNSUPPORTED_REQUEST; the stored why string is the executable-type message, not that token.
attacks.rejected_why: 'LAUNCH_WORKUNIT' is not an executable work type

attacks.detail: validate() iterates sel[:3]. A fourth accepted-or-not item is dropped with n_rejected=0, so the request is not in rejected either.
selected_work as a string is neither list nor dict, so sel becomes []. ok=True, n_rejected=0: the request vanishes.
live_hypotheses are stored on the iteration record but context_pack does not include them, and run() never appends them to k['hypotheses']. The next ask cannot see the resident's own last hypotheses.
COMPUTE is in EXECUTABLE and validate() accepts it. execute() returns ran=False, why='COMPUTE is declared executable but has no runner yet'. Accepted work is not run. Same for READ_RECEIPT.
attacks.execute_why: COMPUTE is declared executable but has no runner yet

attacks.detail: run() breaks the accepted-work loop when the deadline hits and records validation as n_accepted/n_rejected/rejected only. The accepted list itself is not stored, so unlaunched work vanishes.

context_pack uses only the last turn's results_summary[:2], tried_params[-6:], a scar COUNT, and refuted hypothesis ids. 20 iterations of 4000-char summaries do not grow the pack by the history size. The fourteen echo failures were identical-pack, not accumulation.

after one failed-parse turn, LAST TURN is the constant 'no work was accepted from that turn' and tried_params is unchanged. context_pack (and the terse retry pack) is then byte-identical. There is no iteration index, nonce, or prior-reply hash. Under greedy decoding the body returns the same bytes and the loop cannot escape. The fourteen consecutive echoes already happened.

save_kernel uses Path.write_text, which truncates then writes. A crash mid-write leaves a truncated file; the previous kernel is gone. hcli/persist.py::atomic_write_json already does temp + fsync + os.replace and is unused here. The mission kernel is the resident's only memory.
load_kernel json.loads with no handler. A corrupt kernel raises JSONDecodeError, not SovereignRefused, so the next --run crash-loops instead of refusing cleanly.
